claims.content: Player
The software application 'Qheadache' is running on a system meeting the hardware requirements (keyboard, mouse, 800x600 resolution).
A new game has been started or a previous game has been loaded, resulting in the display of the main window.

The game board is displayed, containing a rectangular zone with specific blocks: four square blocks (side x), four rectangular blocks (height 2x, width x), one block (height x, width 2x), and one square block (side 2x).
The blocks are arranged in a configuration that requires the user to move them to solve the headache (puzzle).
The player statistics (block movements, time) are initialized or reset for the current session.
The player selects a block on the game board and initiates a movement.

trigger.raw_text: The player selects a block on the game board and initiates a movement.

claims.content: The player left-clicks on a block to select it.
The game state becomes 'Block displacement'.
The player moves the mouse to drag the selected block across the board.
The system updates the block position in real-time, ensuring it does not overlap other blocks or exit the game zone, and maintains a minimum distance of 0.05x from other blocks.
The player releases the mouse button to place the block at the desired location.
The system records the movement as part of the player statistics (incrementing block movement count and recording time elapsed).
If the large square block (side 2x) is moved to the bottom of the board, the game ends.
The system freezes all player statistics.

If the current player’s block movement count is lower than the highest recorded in the statistic file, the 'Finish Window with Statistics' is displayed; otherwise, the 'Simple Finish Window' is shown.
In the 'Finish Window with Statistics', the player enters their name (up to 20 characters) and clicks 'OK' to save statistics.
The system saves the player’s statistics (name, block movements, time) to the statistic file, replacing the oldest entry if 10 entries already exist.
The 'Finish' window closes and the 'Statistic Window' is displayed, showing the updated list of top 10 player statistics.

If the player clicks 'Undo' from the Action menu (or uses the associated shortcut), the system cancels the last movement. The game displays the block positions as they were before the last movement. This action is unavailable if there was no previous movement.

If the player clicks 'Redo' from the Action menu immediately after an 'Undo' action, the system redoes the canceled movement. The game displays the block positions as they were before the cancellation. This action is unavailable if the previous action was not an 'undo' action.
If the player left-clicks on a selected block while in the 'Block displacement' state, the selection is cancelled, and the game state reverts to 'Block selection'.

If the current player's block movement count is NOT lower than the highest recorded in the statistic file (i.e., the player did not achieve a top score), the 'Simple Finish Window' is displayed instead of the statistics window. This window contains the text 'You win !' and an 'OK' button. Clicking 'OK' closes this window and displays the standard Statistic Window.
If the player attempts to save game statistics or erase statistics and the file cannot be updated due to wrong permissions or a full disk, an error message is displayed.

If the player attempts to exit the game without saving, a dialog box appears asking for confirmation ('Yes' or 'No'). If 'No' is selected, the exit action is cancelled and the main window remains open.
The player statistics (name, block movement count, and time passed) are recorded in the statistic file.
The 'Finish' window is closed.
The Statistic Window is displayed, showing the updated list of top 10 player statistics.
